classification.difficultyReason: Combines signs, zeroes, asymptotes, stationary behaviour and excluded points to identify six reciprocal graph shapes.

content.prompt: Match the graphs in parts (a)–(f) with their reciprocal graphs (I)–(VI).

spec.sourceRegion: Q7 choice I, left column, first choice row
spec.description: Symmetric three-branch curve with positive outer branches, a negative middle maximum and two dashed vertical asymptotes.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled schematic: two excluded vertical lines; positive outside, negative between; outer tails tend to zero. Drawing coordinates and plot expressions are construction parameters, not supplied numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied choice; visible with answers off.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7 choice II, left column, first choice row, right cell
spec.description: Positive symmetric smooth hump with its maximum on the y-axis and both tails approaching the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Unscaled positive curve with a single central maximum and horizontal limit zero; no numerical ticks or grid. Construction coordinates are not question givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied choice; visible with answers off.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7 choice III, left column, second choice row
spec.description: Two negative symmetric branches tending downward without bound at the y-axis and approaching a negative dashed horizontal asymptote from below.
spec.mathematics: Vertical asymptote coincides with the y-axis; both branches are negative. No extra dashed vertical line, ticks, grid or origin label. Construction coordinates are unscaled.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied choice; visible with answers off.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7 choice IV, left column, second choice row, right cell
spec.description: Positive U-shaped central branch between two dashed vertical asymptotes; negative outer branches below a negative dashed horizontal asymptote.
spec.mathematics: Symmetry, three branches, positive middle minimum, negative outer branches and approach to the horizontal asymptote from below. Coordinates are qualitative construction parameters.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied choice; visible with answers off.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7 choice V, top right column, left cell
spec.description: Upward-opening symmetric parabola with a negative vertex and open circles at both apparent x-intercepts.
spec.mathematics: Both points on the x-axis are excluded. White circle interiors are structural masks, not area shading. No numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied choice; visible with answers off.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7 choice VI, top right column, right cell
spec.description: Upward-opening symmetric parabola with its positive minimum on the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: Entirely positive; no x-intercepts, holes, ticks or grid. Construction coordinates do not add numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied choice; visible with answers off.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7(a), first part row, left cell
spec.description: Upward-opening symmetric parabola with a negative vertex and two included x-intercepts.
spec.mathematics: Positive outside its two zeroes, negative between them. No holes, ticks or numerical scale; plot coordinates are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question graph; no response supplied.

answer.worked: I. The two zeroes become vertical asymptotes. Signs are preserved, giving positive outer branches and a negative middle branch with a maximum.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7(b), first part row, right cell
spec.description: Symmetric hump with a positive maximum, two x-intercepts and tails approaching a negative dashed horizontal asymptote from above.
spec.mathematics: Positive between the zeroes and negative outside; nonzero negative horizontal limit. Numerical drawing coordinates are not source givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question graph; no response supplied.

answer.worked: IV. The two zeroes become vertical asymptotes. The positive middle maximum becomes a positive minimum. Negative tails retain their sign and approach a negative reciprocal horizontal asymptote from below.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7(c), second part row, left cell
spec.description: Symmetric negative hump touching the x-axis at its included maximum at the origin, with a negative dashed horizontal asymptote.
spec.mathematics: A touching zero with negative values on both sides; tails approach their negative horizontal limit from above. No origin label or numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question graph; no response supplied.

answer.worked: III. The zero at the origin becomes a vertical asymptote. Both sides remain negative and tend downward without bound near it. The negative horizontal limit becomes a negative reciprocal limit.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7(d), second part row, right cell
spec.description: Positive symmetric smooth hump with a central maximum and tails approaching the x-axis from above.
spec.mathematics: No zeroes; strictly positive with horizontal limit zero. No separately drawn dashed horizontal asymptote, ticks or grid. Coordinates are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question graph; no response supplied.

answer.worked: VI. Positive values remain positive. The maximum becomes a minimum, and the tails approaching zero become large positive values.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7(e), third part row, left cell
spec.description: Upward-opening symmetric parabola with a positive minimum on the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: Entirely positive, with values increasing without bound in both directions. No numerical ticks, grid, holes or origin label.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question graph; no response supplied.

answer.worked: II. The positive minimum becomes a positive maximum. As the original values grow in either direction, the reciprocal approaches zero from above.

spec.sourceRegion: Q7(f), third part row, right cell
spec.description: Symmetric three-branch graph with two dashed vertical asymptotes, positive outer branches and a negative central maximum.
spec.mathematics: Outer branches approach zero outward and positive infinity near the asymptotes; middle branch tends to negative infinity at both asymptotes. No numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question graph; no response supplied.

answer.worked: V. The vertical asymptotes become open circles on the x-axis because the original function is undefined there. Signs are preserved, giving a negative middle section and positive outer sections.
